previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was readmitted due to worsening lower extremity edema and shortness of breath, just days after a prior discharge for similar symptoms. She had a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent cellulitis, and lymphedema. Admission labs showed elevated BNP and white blood cell count, supporting fluid overload and possible infection. She was treated with IV furosemide and metolazone for aggressive diuresis, resulting in a weight loss from 151.1 kg to 144.8 kg. IV vancomycin was continued for a full 7-day course due to persistent leg redness and warmth, with improvement by discharge. Hypokalemia developed during diuresis and was managed with supplementation. Her phenytoin level rose to 26.1, prompting a dose reduction to 700 mg daily. Warfarin was increased to achieve a therapeutic INR of 2.0. She was discharged home with medication adjustments, instructions to monitor daily weight, and plans for outpatient lab follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with chronic HFpEF, chronic 
lymphedema, recent lower extremity cellulitis, DVT's, and 
seizure disorder on dilantin who presents with confusion and new 
tremor concerning for dilantin toxicity.  
 
# Dilantin toxicity: Patient with symptoms of subjective 
confusion, tremor, nystagmus, and ataxia, which were concerning 
for dilantin toxicity. Dilantin level on admission 22.2 on 
admission. Supratherapeutic level likely due to increased 
medication absorption in the setting of decreased bowel edema 
with diuresis during last admission as well as increasing 
warfarin dose. Neurology was consulted and felt that sx 
consistent with dilantin toxicity. They noted that symptoms 
could last for up to a few weeks, even once levels have returned 
back to therapeutic levels. Per neurology, patient switched to 
Keppra 1500 BID ___ and dilantin discontinued. Patient's 
symptoms, including confusion, tremor, and nystagmus, improved 
throughout the course of her admission. Additionally, due to her 
initial complaints of ataxia, she was evaluated by Physical 
Therapy who felt that she was safe for discharge. The patient 
will follow-up with outpatient Neurology at ___ for ongoing 
AED monitoring.  

# Seizure disorder: In terms of seizure history, she usually has 
generalized tonic clonic seizures, but on her recent admission 
in ___ she was noted to possibly have a partial complex 
seizure. During this current admission, there was a question of 
another partial complex seizure with brief bilateral upper 
extremity shaking. Patient underwent continued vEEG monitoring x 
24 hours without any evidence of seizure activity. Neurology 
team also felt that it would have been extremely unlikely for 
the patient to have had a seizure while still therapeutic on 
dilantin and on keppra and topomax. As above, patient will 
follow-up with outpatient Neurology at ___ for ongoing AED 
monitoring.  

# History of DVT, PE: INR slightly sub-therapeutic on admission 
at 1.9. INR downtrended throughout the course of admission, 
likely due to withdrawal of dilantin. Unclear if patient really 
needs anticoagulation as DVT was ___ years ago, but given 
sub-therapeutic levels, warfarin increased from 5 mg PO QD to at 
8 mg PO QD. INR should be trended carefully as an outpatient, as 
removal of phenytoin can increase INR. INR at discharge 2.1. INR 
should be rechecked on ___.

# Chronic HFpEF: Recent discharge weight: 144.8 kg, down from 
151.5 kg on last admission. Patient complained of upper

was give one extra dose of lasix 160 mg IV with improvement in
